standard_prerequisites.name: Additivity of divisors for a restricted family
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-additivity-divisors-restricted, invoked at proof line 4419
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final identity expressing a length over the local ring as the sum over its minimal primes of the local length times the length after quotienting by the prime, which is exactly the coefficient comparison the proof needs.

core_obligations: Reduce to a coefficient comparison at the generic point of an integral Z of delta-dimension k: choose a generator of the invertible module at that point, write the section as f times that generator, so that hypothesis (3) becomes the injectivity of multiplication by f on the local ring A, and note that the coefficient in the cycle of the zero scheme is length_A(A/(f)) (proof lines 4381-4395).

Dispose of the zero-dimensional case: if the local ring has dimension zero, injectivity of multiplication by f forces f to be a unit, so the coefficient is zero, while the same dimension hypothesis says that the point lies on no component of dimension k + 1 and hence the coefficient on the other side is zero too (proof lines 4397-4402).

Conclude in the one-dimensional case: the minimal primes of A correspond bijectively to the components passing through the point, the multiplicities in the cycle of Y are the lengths of the localisations, and the multiplicity of the class of Z in the cycle of the restricted zero scheme is the length after quotienting by the prime; the required equality of lengths is then precisely the additivity statement for divisors (proof lines 4404-4420).
proof_roadmap: Turn the assertion into a comparison of two coefficients in a one-dimensional local ring (proof lines 4381-4395).
Handle the zero-dimensional case by invertibility of the local equation (proof lines 4397-4402).
Match the length with the sum over the minimal primes by the additivity lemma (proof lines 4404-4420).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the cycle of the zero scheme of a global section with the sum over the components of Y of the multiplicities times the cycles of the restricted sections, under the hypothesis that the section is injective at every generic point of the k-dimensional part of its zero scheme (statement lines 4357-4379, tag 0EPI). The proof is a local computation: it chooses a generator at the generic point of an integral Z so that the section becomes an element f of the local ring A, splits off the zero-dimensional case where injectivity forces f to be a unit, and in the one-dimensional case matches the length of A/(f) with the sum over the minimal primes of the local length times the length of A/(f, q_i). That matching is the substance, so the claim is H2.
